title: Assign Cookies
description: You are given two integer arrays g and s, where g[i] is the greed factor of the ith child, and s[j] is the size of the jth cookie. Each child i can be satisfied with at most one cookie if the cookie's size is greater than or equal to the child's greed factor. Return the maximum number of children that can be content.
constraints: Each cookie can be assigned to at most one child

examples.explanation: With cookies of size 1 and 1, only the child with greed factor 1 can be satisfied.
Both children can be satisfied since there are cookies large enough for each.

title: Lemonade Change
description: At a lemonade stand, each lemonade costs $5. Customers are standing in a queue to buy from you and order one at a time (in the order specified by bills). Each customer will only buy one lemonade and pay with either a $5, $10, or $20 bill. You must provide the correct change to each customer so that the net transaction is that the customer pays $5. You start with no change on hand. Given an integer array bills where bills[i] is the bill the ith customer pays, return true if you can provide every customer with the correct change, or false otherwise.
constraints: You start with zero bills of any denomination
Change must be provided using only $5 and $10 bills you have collected

examples.explanation: Each customer receives correct change using the bills collected so far.
By the time the last customer pays with 20, there aren't enough $5 bills left to give change.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
description: You are given an integer array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day. On each day, you may decide to buy and/or sell the stock. You can only hold at most one share of the stock at any time. However, you can buy it then immediately sell it on the same day. Find and return the maximum profit you can achieve.
constraints: You may complete as many transactions as you like
You cannot engage in multiple transactions simultaneously

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price=1) and sell on day 3 (price=5), profit = 4. Then buy on day 4 (price=3) and sell on day 5 (price=6), profit = 3. Total profit = 7.
Buy on day 1 (price=1) and sell on day 5 (price=5), profit = 4.

title: Maximum Number of Non-Overlapping Intervals to Remove
description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping. Intervals that only touch at the endpoint are not considered overlapping.
constraints: Intervals may overlap partially or fully

examples.explanation: Removing [1,3] leaves the rest of the intervals non-overlapping.
You need to remove two of the three [1,2] intervals to make the remaining one non-overlapping.

title: Maximum 69 Number
description: Given a positive integer num consisting only of digits 6 and 9, return the maximum number you can get by changing at most one digit (6 becomes 9, or 9 becomes 6).
constraints: num consists of only digits 6 and 9
At most one digit can be changed
The number does not have leading zeros

examples.explanation: Changing the first 6 to a 9 gives the maximum possible number, 9969.
Changing the last digit 6 to 9 gives the maximum possible number, 9999.
